newsitem.title: USA: Dow struts to fourth straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Dow struts to fourth straight record close.

text.p: Blue chip stocks extended their relentless rally on Wednesday, powering the Dow Jones industrial average to its fourth consecutive record finish.

The Dow climbed 36.56 to close at 7,575.83, surpassing the previous all-time high of 7,539.27 on Tuesday. In the broader market, advancers outpaced decliners 1,509 to 1,024 on heavy volume of 513.7 million on the New York Stock Exchange. More than 500 million shares changed hands for the second day in a row.
The broad rally lifted large-cap and small-cap indexes and saw technology stocks reverse Tuesday's losses.
The Nasdaq composite index, laden with technology shares, rose 6.16 points to 1,407.85.
"The rest of the market just seems to be tagging along behind the blue chips," said Hildegard Zagorski, market analyst at Prudential Securities.
Beyond the tech stocks, which erased early losses to end higher, the market was a model of calm, an atmosphere that stood in stark contrast to the volatility of the recent past.

"The market appears to be settling down after its rapid acceleration," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co. "But the bulls just continue to dominate, and it looks like this could be the tilt for a while."

Cyclical stocks, particularly shares in paper and pulp companies, were among the best performers. International Paper Co. rose 5/8 to 50-3/8 after announcing price increases on certain grades of pulp effective next month.

The move was matched by competitors such as Weyerhaeuser Co. and Champion International Corp. and was viewed as an early sign that market conditions are finally improving for the beleaguered industry. Weyerhaeuser shares jumped 2-7/8 to 53-3/8 and Champion gained 1/2 to 49-1/8.

While the market shows no clear signs of halting in its advance, analysts said some kind of pause certainly appears due, with the Dow industrials now up a sizzling 18.5 percent -- or nearly 1,200 points -- in the last two months.
"You could have a pullback any time here," Zagorski said, adding the Dow "could easily come down a couple of hundred points, but even that wouldn't make a bit of difference to its long-term trend."
Among individual issues, Numar Corp. soared 16-3/16 to 36-15/16 after agreeing to be acquired by Halliburton Co.
Under terms of the deal announced late Tuesday, Halliburton will swap 0.4832 of a share for each Numar share. Halliburton, an energy services company, fell 1-3/4 to 79-1/8.
Lennar Corp. jumped 4-1/4 to 30-5/8 after announcing it would spin off its finance business and then merge with fellow home-building company Greystone Corp. Greystone shares slipped 2 to 15-1/8.
Student loan financing company Sallie Mae surged 6-1/8 to 126-3/8 after Sallie Mae's chief executive announced plans to step down.
Analysts said they were hopeful the move was a sign that a months-long battle for control of the company was headed for a compromise conclusion.
Eastman Kodak Co. slid 4-1/4 to 79-5/8. Analysts expressed concern about pricing pressure faced by the company in the U.S. film industry from Fuji Photo Film Co.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 4.30 points to 869.57, a record. The American Stock Exchange index edged up 1.56 to 622.67.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.74 to 453.50, a record. The average price per share rose 16 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues also known as the Wilshire 5000 -- was a record 8,227.145, up 32.38, or 0.40 percent.
